x: The Walk gave us an opportunity of seeing Brown at his best, and it was a very fine effort which gained second place for him. Victory went to "Doug" Earle, one of our recent newcomers, and he should repeat this success many times in future races despite shortening marks.

Rutland can do better than the time he recorded on this occasion. The fifth man, "Doug" Earle, with a 5-min. allowance, carried off the sealed handicap, with Frank Jarvis, who followed him in, and with the same allowance, second.
True, off 675 yards, won the 2 Miles Walk in easy fashion, with Doug. Earle second, and G.

Douglas Earle walked splendidly and his fastest race yet to take second position; with George Boddington repeating his good walking of our "Open" event and being placed third.
Doug. Earle, who used to race in the days of Len Fletcher and Don Brown, for they all worked at the same firm, is now in the R.A.F., stationed at Tangmere.
Joe Flower writes from Somerset sending best wishes to all of his old friends. Doug. Earle has done no racing for several years, owing to heart-strain.
